issue_title: Presets: emit industry-appropriate itemTypes so customer contact forms don't fall back to the generic default list
problem_statement:
Presets: emit industry-appropriate itemTypes so customer contact forms don't fall back to the generic default list

Split from #316 (residual 4 of its 2026-08-01 diagnosis — filed there as "undecided"; this issue is the decision surface plus the build once settled).

## Problem

0 of 8 presets in `apps/mcp/content/presets/` declare `itemTypes` (verified against main @ 52db1d1). The template's contact route consumes `site.itemTypes` for its dropdown and fail-closed validation; without it, every preset-rendered customer site serves the generic default list — DR#2 showed this is also what red-ed the contact-route test fixtures before template#15 decoupled them.

## Contract sketch (session-sized once shaped)

- Each of the 8 presets gains an `itemTypes` array appropriate to its industry (e.g. hvac: repair / installation / maintenance-plan / estimate-request classes), flowing through `render_site_ts` into the rendered config.
- Renderer/schema: confirm `render_site_ts` passes `itemTypes` through (add if missing) and `validateSiteConfig` accepts it (it does — top-level optional).
- Sensor: presets test asserting every preset ships a non-empty `itemTypes`; render test asserting pass-through.

## Judgment-call note for the implementer/reviewer

These strings are customer-facing dropdown copy on rendered sites. Presets already carry driver-authored customer-facing strings (services, FAQ), so this stays a driver-workable Tier B lane — but the reviewer should read the strings as copy, not just data. Unrelated and untouched: the Beehiiv "Visibility waitlist" itemType label (standing do-not-touch, lesson 26).

## Acceptance criteria

1. All 8 presets ship non-empty industry-appropriate `itemTypes`.
2. Pass-through verified render → template contact route (config-parity style test).
3. Full gate green both packages.
